solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seeks sustenance over a long time

parts.note: over the weekend means for the weekend, a span of time
ages is everyday speech for a long while

explanation.surface: An animal hunts for its food over a long stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase the wordplay is FOR AGES, which means over a long time; closed up it becomes a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food, so an animal that forages seeks sustenance.

clue.text: Furniture has notice inside square base

indicators.note: the square base has the notice inside it, between its two parts

parts.note: four is the square of two
a bed is a base, as a flower bed or the bed of a road
a poster is a printed notice put up on a wall

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture carries a notice set into its square base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is a number here: two squared is four. 'Has' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with a post at each corner holding a canopy is a large item of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Power in sacred object and a copy

indicators.note: the letter for power goes in the word for a sacred object

parts.note: a relic is a holy object, such as a saint's bone
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A sacred relic holds power, and someone has made a copy of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction, a duplicate made of an original.

clue.text: Blood round end of fingers, after touching this?

definitions.text: Blood round end of fingers, after touching this?

indicators.note: the word for blood goes round the letter taken from fingers

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: the end of the word fingers is its final letter

explanation.surface: Blood ends up round your fingertips after you touch a prickly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: gorse is so spiny that touching it can leave blood round the fingertips.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, also called furze, is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub whose thorns draw blood when grasped.

clue.text: Rhinestone, a national symbol

definitions.meaning: the three-leaved clover is the emblem of Ireland

explanation.surface: A rhinestone held up as a country's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SHAM ROCK, the word describes a rhinestone, a fake gem; whole, it is Ireland's plant emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The trefoil clover worn on St Patrick's Day is the emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: A person barely to be seen on such a beach?

definitions.text: A person barely to be seen on such a beach?

parts.words: A person barely to be seen on such a beach?
parts.note: barely plays on bare: someone seen unclothed on a naturist beach

explanation.surface: Someone hardly ever spotted at a particular kind of seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to mean hardly ever; it really means in the bare, wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed, and is seen bare on a clothing-optional beach.

clue.text: Slip carelessly on treacherous surface, not a success

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to nod is to make a careless slip, as even Homer nods
ice is a slippery and dangerous surface

explanation.surface: Someone slips carelessly on an icy surface, and the outing is a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no dice' means no luck or no go, so an attempt that fails.

clue.text: Group under attack puts off accepting downfall

indicators.note: the word for puts off takes in the word for downfall

parts.note: defers means postpones
an end is a downfall or demise

explanation.surface: A beleaguered group delays matters before accepting their downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The side being attacked is the one guarding its position, as in sport or war.

clue.text: To lacerate is frightening, if poking inside

indicators.note: the word if pokes into the middle of the word for frightening

parts.note: scary means frightening

explanation.surface: Lacerating is frightening if something sharp is poking inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarify is to make scratches or small cuts in skin, so to tear or wound it.

clue.text: Worker on drug getting advantage

indicators.note: the worker comes on after the drug in the across order

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a hand is a manual worker, as a farm hand

explanation.surface: A labourer high on drugs gains an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the upper hand is to hold the controlling position over a rival.

clue.text: Money is spurned by saint

indicators.note: the word is is rejected by the saint's name, dropped from it

parts.note: St Francis of Assisi is the best-known saint of that name

explanation.surface: A holy man rejects cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suits St Francis, who gave up his wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and Belgium, and remains the Swiss unit.

clue.text: First takes this money order, revolutionary symbol

parts.note: a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money
the red flag is the emblem of socialist revolution

explanation.surface: A winner accepts a cheque and waves a revolutionary banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is the race winner: the black and white flag is waved as the leader crosses the line.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing the flag of black and white squares greets the winning car at the finish.

clue.text: One has to ask about balance

indicators.note: the word for to ask goes about the numeral for one

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One must ask a question about the balance of an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is steadiness and composure, an even balance of body or mind.

clue.text: Obscure eastern doctrine recollected

indicators.note: re-collected, the letters gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: A little-known Oriental creed is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' looks like remembered; split as re-collected it rearranges E and DOCTRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is abstruse, known only to a few specialists.

clue.text: Long ago got onto small problem for horse

indicators.note: the phrase for long ago is attached onto the end of the letter for small

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing
way back is informal for long ago

explanation.surface: Long ago someone tackled a minor difficulty with a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A swayback is an abnormally sagging spine in a horse, a defect of its back.

clue.text: With some footballers, speed is key

parts.note: backs are defensive players in football
pace means speed

explanation.surface: For certain footballers, speed is the crucial quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning crucial; it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard key that moves the cursor back and deletes is a typing key.

clue.text: Cheers poker challenge?

definitions.meaning: cheers is a casual goodbye, like cheerio or bye for now
in poker a player matches a bet to call an opponent's hand

explanation.surface: A toast at the card table as one player calls another's bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a casual parting word and the poker call of matching a rival's stake.

clue.text: Excellent spinner cut

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a notch is a small cut

explanation.surface: A spin bowler is praised for a superb delivery that cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal term for first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Await half-suppressed spits

indicators.note: the second half of the word for spits is held back, leaving the first

parts.note: expectorates means coughs up and spits

explanation.surface: Someone waits while partly holding back spitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-suppressed' keeps the first half of EXPECTORATES and suppresses ORATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect is to look forward to or anticipate, much like waiting for something.

clue.text: Model piece of text shortly disappeared

parts.note: para is short for paragraph

indicators.note: said short, the word for disappeared loses its final letter

parts.note: gone means vanished

explanation.surface: A model passage of writing has vanished in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example to follow.

clue.text: Think right, following Tory party

indicators.note: the letter for right follows the other two pieces

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a side is one party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A right-winger reflects on following the Tory party line.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to think something over, to reflect upon it.

clue.text: Drop mark? Managed to keep it

indicators.note: the word for managed holds on to the word for mark

parts.note: did means managed, as in did well
a scar is a mark left on skin

explanation.surface: Should one remove a blemish, or manage to keep it?
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to throw away or drop, as with an unwanted card.

clue.text: River's course under the sea

definitions.note: read as river is, the 's being the verb

indicators.note: in a down clue the course sits under the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
a way is a course or route

explanation.surface: A river's channel runs beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Medway is a river in Kent, south-east England, flowing into the Thames estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medway is an English river, running through Kent past Maidstone and Rochester.

clue.text: Composer's Swiss mug?

definitions.note: read as composer is, the 's being the verb

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital, standing for something Swiss
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A composer owns a beer mug from Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss mug' is read as a mug from the Swiss capital: a Bern stein.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was the American composer of West Side Story.

clue.text: Second-hand book starts to get you transported

indicators.note: the letter for book starts the word, coming before the rest

parts.note: used means second-hand

explanation.surface: A second-hand book begins to move you emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests rapture; it means carried by bus. The single-S spelling is the less common but accepted form.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bused is to be carried by coach or omnibus, conveyed from place to place.

clue.text: Number five brought into the world, inhaling oxygen

indicators.note: the word for brought into the world breathes in the symbol for oxygen

parts.note: born means given birth to
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A fifth child is born and takes its first breath of oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical element with atomic number 5 is a metalloid, symbol B.

clue.text: Drug, said to give Macbeth hallucination

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so a word sounding like it is entered

parts.note: Macbeth sees a phantom dagger before he murders Duncan

explanation.surface: A narcotic is claimed to give Macbeth his vision.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the r of the weapon is silent, so it rhymes with the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagga is the South African word for cannabis.

clue.text: Force wife, after adjusting, to meet everyone

indicators.note: the letters of after are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A wife is made, after some coercion, to meet everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a placing word but is the fodder for 'adjusting', giving ATERF. 'Force' is northern English (from Norse) for a waterfall, as in Aira Force in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a force is a cascade, a usage found in Lake District place names.

clue.text: One of seven enzymes failing out of medium

indicators.note: the enzymes break down, so their letters fall into disorder
the letter for medium is taken out of the word

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing

explanation.surface: Something from a set of seven enzymes fails outside a culture medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' removes M from ENZYMES, and 'failing' rearranges the remaining ENZYES.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven are the Dwarfs of Disney's Snow White, one of whom keeps sneezing.

clue.text: Abashed, wait to make good

parts.note: to hang about or hang on is to wait
do means make, as in do a meal

explanation.surface: Someone ashamed waits for the chance to make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make good' reads as making amends, but splits into DO for make and G for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and guilty, like a dog that knows it has misbehaved.
